panels.rationale: Single AP chest radiograph from a patient with vanishing lung syndrome (article title and prior triage agree). It is a real patient image, not a diagram or control, and the caption attributes bilateral upper-lobe bullous emphysema (severe in the left hemithorax, arrow) to vanishing lung syndrome rather than another disease. The hyperlucent avascular left hemithorax and giant upper-lobe bullae match vocabulary findings; no mediastinal shift or diaphragmatic inversion is clearly stated or seen, so those are not claimed. Minor blunting of the left costophrenic angle (small effusion/pleural thickening) reported in-text is not in the vocabulary and is listed as a proposed finding.
